rationale: Most literal ground-truth bugs (NaN ordering, zip strict=True, ClassVar AttributeError, absent-vs-empty schedule, boundary-vs-step counting, Ref2VA schedule reuse) are already fixed in this final diff, so neither candidate can 'recall' them verbatim; what matters is who finds the closest residual analogs. Y catches the sharpest one — default_video_shift/audio_shift still sourced only from the FL2VA release and applied to the Ref2VA base_schedule, a direct echo of the PR's central per-partition-scoping concern — plus a real NaN bypass in shifted_sigmas and a legitimate test-coverage gap (diffuse stubbed, real denoise-loop conversion untested), all with precise line-level evidence. X's review is well-verified in places (ran tests, checked denoise_loop math) but its headline 'wrong package' finding recommends reverting sigma_schedule.py out of diffusion/sched/ — exactly the move a real reviewer explicitly requested and got implemented — which is a confident, well-argued but factually contradicted claim that hurts precision. Both are highly actionable with file/line anchors; Y edges ahead on precision and relevance to the actual review history.
